bug_semantics: Iterator.concat in quickjs.c is a C iterator helper that stores pending iterable objects and their @@iterator methods in it->values. js_iterator_concat_next takes pointers into that array (obj/meth) and calls JS_GetIterator2 on them before setting it->running, so user JS can re-enter. The published PoC (issue #1368) does it.return() from a hostile @@iterator; js_iterator_concat_return then walks the remaining it->values and JS_FreeValue's each slot without replacing it with JS_UNDEFINED. When concat_next resumes it still holds the stale obj/meth pointers and, after the inner iterator reports done, JS_FreeValue's *meth/*obj again (and the ASAN trace is a heap use-after-free in free_gc_object via js_free_value_rt). CVE-2026-3979 names js_iterator_concat_return; CNA CWE-416 / GHSA also lists CWE-119. Attack is local script in the engine. Advisory scope is 0.12.0–0.12.1 (text: up to 0.12.1); the same sink is present from the Iterator.concat introduction through v0.12.1 and is patched on master by daab4ad (v0.13.0).
flaw_origin: The free-without-nulling loop in js_iterator_concat_return and the unguarded JS_GetIterator2 on pointers into it->values in js_iterator_concat_next were first written together in PR #1158 member ef8dc076e01803d85cd5c771c289842fc2e18a47 ('Add Iterator.concat', Ben Noordhuis, 2025-09-23/24), implementing the TC39 iterator-sequencing proposal. The sibling member 8d2a1eb95e9c39b632dd467ad6f502d1039aeb08 only regenerates codegen binaries. reasoning: CVE-2026-3979 is a real, published use-after-free in QuickJS-ng Iterator.concat, not a withdrawn or rejected advisory. The sink is the combination of (1) js_iterator_concat_next holding pointers into it->values across a user-controlled JS_GetIterator2 call made before the running guard, and (2) js_iterator_concat_return freeing those slots without poisoning them, so the resumed next path double-releases the same JSValues.
